Measure m120 at 5/1, 50 uL, predicted V1/V2 26.58/60.88 mL. At 150 uL, observed 20913a7c2077b80b7351 gave 13.90/72.41, with historical V2 underprediction of 40.71 mL. This matched loading contrast tests whether early onset and a broad elution interval persist at lower sample amount; current predictions are almost load-invariant.

Measure m120 at 2/1, 150 uL, predicted 20.13/31.28 mL. Relative to measured 5/1 row 20913a7c2077b80b7351, this holds loading fixed and tests the predicted earlier onset at the weaker 5/1 eluent alongside much later completion. Together with the selected loading contrast, it separates solvent response from loading sensitivity.

Measure pyridyl ketone m66 at 2/1, 100 uL, predicted 18.17/37.15 mL. Its measured 1/1 row 8f5acbec0c511bb1ea89 gave 12.23/34.83 despite a historical V2 prediction of 17.15. This matched solvent contrast tests whether retraining has learned broad intervals across conditions or only corrected one anchor; ethyl nicotinate reference 6a4e95d2a3cca31094a1 provides related nitrogen-carbonyl chemistry.

Measure p-aminobenzonitrile m160 at 2/1, 50 uL, predicted 22.02/42.35 mL. Same-load observations a8ae74aecb3b1e85b73c and ad833f34f6b91872362d span 6.18/19.48 at 1/1 to 44.72/101.17 at 5/1. This intermediate point locates the steep rise after the large 5/1 underprediction and complements pending pure-EA supervision.

Measure m-aminobenzonitrile m161 at 5/1, 50 uL, predicted 31.60/67.30 mL. Measured e12edd0198c0d750ecd5 at 2/1 gave 14.22/31.49 at the same loading. Comparison with para-isomer ad833f34f6b91872362d at identical 5/1 loading tests positional-isomer transfer despite identical coarse polarity descriptors.

Measure methylquinoline m146 at 5/1, 50 uL, predicted 37.42/70.99 mL. Same-load 2/1 reference cf36dbeee8bb51632d84 gave 20.07/34.11; recent 10/1 row 9e3ce3497298084abd83 reached 59.58/106.50 at 100 uL. This tests response curvature between anchors, with the upper anchor's loading difference retained.

Measure benzyl-substituted beta-ketoester m78 at 20/1, 100 uL, predicted 31.84/59.64 mL. Recent same-load 50/1 observation 61771d230b285babe4b6 gave 49.93/97.97 and was substantially underpredicted; 10/1 reference b5e6e9a4b5c6f0f838bd was much earlier at a different load. This locates the rise and tests transfer among beta-ketoesters alongside pending m25 and m94 measurements.

Measure m53 at 20/1, 100 uL, predicted 21.86/46.37 mL. Recent 5/1 and 10/1 observations 702ba575d6a3442b9a3b and 30970941542856ce8eb1 were much earlier than predicted, whereas 50/1 row cdc8c1db00222994a1aa reached 30.61/70.14. This tests whether the rise now occurs at the correct ratio, matching the 50/1 anchor's loading while acknowledging the lower loads of the intermediate anchors.

Measure methyl acetoacetate m95 at 20/1, 50 uL, predicted 18.38/42.81 mL. Measured 150-uL row d448d8de2d8dacec62c3 gave 15.69/48.54, with historical V2 underprediction of 22.96 mL. This matched loading contrast tests whether completion remains late at lower loading and informs transfer to pending cyclopropyl beta-ketoester m94 at 20/1.

Measure diphenyl sulfoxide m199 at 10/1, 150 uL, predicted 30.04/47.96 mL. Measured same-load 5/1 row 6bd128bde2e137ea54f3 gave 27.42/52.38, so the model predicts earlier completion in weaker eluent. Three measured 5/1 loads have nearly constant completion, making this solvent contrast more informative than further loading replication. It tests whether the predicted reversal is real.

Measure previously unlabeled naphthylethanol m205 at 5/1, 100 uL, predicted 12.19/22.69 mL. Methoxyphenethyl alcohol 776ee2c1e85ebde75168 at the same ratio and sample volume gave 48.00/77.09, while naphthylmethanol 7c0c324643799c918828 was accurately predicted at 2/1. This tests alcohol-family transfer and complements pending m206 at 10/1; ring attachment, hydroxyl spacing, and loading details differ.

Measure ether-bearing aryl ketone m106 at 10/1, 100 uL, predicted 35.24/67.87 mL. Measured b1c5816f929ef59f5a87 at 20/1 gave 41.72/79.81, while ed763ea5943e63a671c9 at 1/1 gave 6.23/10.54 under matching loading conditions. This tests the inferred onset of strong retention in an ether-carbonyl environment, extending response learning beyond beta-ketoesters.

Measure previously unlabeled 3-phenylpropanal m183 at 20/1, 50 uL, predicted 14.50/23.22 mL. Its flexible aldehyde environment provides a structural transfer test after m53 showed misplaced solvent response in 30970941542856ce8eb1. Measured phenylpropanol 53c1be5b96937954b9fa supplies a related carbon skeleton, although functional group and conditions differ. This tests carbonyl-environment effects versus a generic aldehyde response.

Measure previously unlabeled mesityl methyl ketone m29 at 20/1, 50 uL, predicted 7.13/26.06 mL. Two ortho methyl groups plausibly modify silica access to the carbonyl. Observed ortho-methyl acetophenone 918504cfbad81b27c08e and dimethyl acetophenone c356230277dfc98406e0 show different endpoint patterns under other conditions. This tests transfer within the recurring aryl-ketone family without assuming a steric retention ordering.

Measure methyl benzoylformate m92 at 1/1, 50 uL, loaded in 200 uL EA, predicted 6.75/22.06 mL. Pair with the selected PE-loaded row to isolate loading-solvent identity. Observed EA-loaded e93e08d6bc42e91e2679 at 100 uL gave 10.24/25.15, while 9768d61b571fc0c5ce1a at 2/1 and 50 uL gave 8.41/17.03. This also establishes a fixed-load mobile-phase contrast.

Measure m92 at 1/1, 50 uL, loaded in 200 uL PE, predicted 6.48/21.48 mL. The selected EA-loaded counterpart differs only in loading-solvent identity, yet predicted endpoints differ by less than 0.6 mL. This clean contrast tests the model's weak solvent sensitivity in an alpha-ketoester with broad observed intervals; neither the direction nor magnitude of an injection-solvent effect is established.

hypotheses.content: Diethyl malonate's fast completion at weak eluents is reproducible across the supplied 20/1 and 50/1 observations, although its elution interval remains finite.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The original large failure now has corroborating labels. Additional near-duplicate weak-eluent measurements have lower marginal value than unresolved response regions elsewhere; this exception should not be generalized to all diesters.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: If future predictions fail at stronger eluents or in substituted malonates, does the fast response remain molecule-specific?

hypotheses.content: Late-retention anchors do not reliably determine the location or shape of the solvent-response rise; intermediate labels can correct premature rises and missed steep transitions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Historical overprediction at intermediate ratios and underprediction at weaker eluents show that molecule-level offsets alone are insufficient. Learning response shape can improve several remaining conditions per molecule and related families.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do selected intermediate m53, m78, m146, m160, and m106 rows support the current rise locations, and does sulfoxide really finish earlier at 10/1 than at 5/1?

hypotheses.content: Sample loading has compound- and endpoint-specific effects; near-invariant completion in sulfoxide does not establish invariance for broad alcohol or beta-ketoester intervals.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The predictor remains almost invariant across sample amounts, whereas measured onset shifts can be appreciable even when completion changes little. Targeted contrasts can teach when this invariance is appropriate and when separate endpoint responses are needed.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed eluent and loading-solvent conditions, do m120 and m95 retain broad intervals at 50 uL, and which endpoint changes most?

hypotheses.content: Functional-group environment and positional substitution can alter onset and completion differently, limiting transfer based on coarse polarity or a single alcohol, nitrogen, or carbonyl category.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Recent exploration found severe V2 failures for methoxy alcohols and a pyridyl ketone, but accurate predictions for naphthylmethanol and an aromatic diketone. Selective analog measurements can distinguish transferable chemistry from isolated corrections.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected alcohol, aminonitrile, pyridyl-ketone, flexible-aldehyde, and hindered-ketone measurements reveal systematic structure-condition differences beyond current predictions?

hypotheses.content: Loading-solvent identity may contribute to m92's endpoint behavior, but existing observations do not isolate this effect and the model predicts a small PE-versus-EA difference.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A matched PE/EA loading-solvent pair tests an input relationship otherwise confounded with sample amount or mobile phase. Either a substantial effect or a small effect provides useful supervision for the condition representation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 1/1 mobile phase, 50 uL sample volume, and a 200-uL loading plug, do PE and EA loading solvents produce materially different V1 or V2?

feedback_interpretation: The malonate follow-up supported fast weak-eluent completion: new 20/1 and 50/1 rows finished at 8.54 and 8.27 mL, with acquisition endpoint errors no greater than 1.26 mL. Further dense sampling there has lower priority. The m53 follow-up showed that the inferred rise occurred too early: 5/1 and 10/1 completion was overpredicted by 13.64 and 24.21 mL. The oxime 20/1 CW outcome similarly weakened extrapolation from its late 50/1 anchor. Conversely, recent CW measurements exposed substantial underprediction for m78, m146, and m160, motivating intermediate response measurements. Structural exploration was selective in its failures: m120 finished at 72.41 mL despite a 31.70 prediction, m119 at 77.09 despite 36.16, and m66 at 34.83 despite 17.15; m206 and m178 were already accurate at acquisition. Sulfoxide completion stayed near 52 mL across three measured loads, and anisaldehyde's new loading point was reasonably predicted. The near-matched cinnamic-acid 5/1 loading plugs gave 11.88/61.87 and 12.92/60.92 mL, weakening a large plug-volume explanation at that condition without establishing universal invariance. These are historical acquisition errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The pending set already supplies polar response points, two amino-benzoate conditions, a methoxyphenethyl-alcohol intermediate, and weak-eluent checks for nitrile, ether, and ketone families. The supplements add matched m120 and m95 loading contrasts, an isolated m92 loading-solvent comparison, intermediate solvent points around recent failures, and structural comparisons with measured anchors. The two m120 measurements are complementary: one changes loading at fixed mobile phase, while the other changes mobile phase at fixed loading. The aminonitrile measurements connect same-load response curves and positional-isomer behavior. Three previously unlabeled structures test transfer in recurring alcohol, aldehyde, and aryl-ketone environments. Further replication of recently accurate malonate and sulfoxide loading responses is deferred. Quantile widths and CW distances are secondary evidence, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty; broad elution intervals are target behavior. The batch aims to improve both endpoints across the Row-distribution by teaching response shape and conditional structural effects, without assuming unrecorded experimental variables.
